items.item: ORC's row-index advantage over Parquet in this topic's measurement is a function of the row-group size chosen, not an inherent property of either format — a Parquet writer that sets a 10,000-row row group matches ORC's own granularity exactly.

at.step: Reveal: ORC's fixed index beats a bare row-group default

items.item: The index-byte accounting in this topic is a simplification (a fixed per-entry size for both formats); the comparison that holds regardless of the exact constant is the relative one: ten entries, versus four, versus forty.

ORC's index streams being placed first in the stripe is a locality decision, not a different feature from Parquet's footer-based metadata — both formats put their statistics somewhere a reader can consult before touching the bulk of the data.

at.step: Reveal: ORC's stripe and stream layout

items.item: Hive's row-level ACID transactions were explicitly designed to be format-agnostic (any format with a row id could in principle support them); ORC becoming the only supported format was an integration-effort decision, not a design requirement of the feature itself.

at.step: Reveal: ORC's ACID history in Hive

items.item: External tables cannot be ACID tables in Hive because the compactor, which does the actual merge work, has no control over files it doesn't manage — a constraint of the compaction architecture, not an arbitrary restriction.

'Parquet became the lakehouse default' is a claim about ecosystem adoption, not a claim that ORC's own technical design is inferior — this topic's own index comparison shows ORC winning the bare-default case.

at.step: Reveal: why Parquet became the lakehouse default anyway

items.item: This topic's own forward reference to the table formats of the next section (Delta Lake, Iceberg, Hudi choosing Parquet) is a fact about what's coming in this chapter, not a claim this topic's own sources independently verify about those specific projects.

at.step: Reveal: why Parquet became the lakehouse default anyway

items.item: ORC still appearing in legacy Hive and some Trino estates is a statement about where ORC is read today, not a claim that new ORC-format tables are commonly created going forward.

at.step: Reveal: why Parquet became the lakehouse default anyway

items.item: The Bloom Filter Index that ORC added from Hive 1.2.0 onward is a further, separate opt-in structure beyond the row index this topic measures — named in this topic's own sources but not built here, consistent with keeping this topic's lab scope to the row-pruning comparison its outcomes actually name.
The 200MB figure for a typical ORC stripe is itself described by the spec as typical, not fixed — unlike the 10,000-row row-group default, stripe size is a writer-tunable parameter in practice.
